title: The 'Best Time to Post' Myth, and What Actually Matters More
content:
Search "best time to post on Instagram" and you'll find a dozen conflicting charts, each claiming a different golden hour. The truth is less exciting: for most accounts, timing matters far less than people assume.

What the data actually shows

Modern feed algorithms are built around relevance, not recency. A great post published at a mediocre time will still get surfaced to interested users over the following hours and days. A mediocre post at a perfect time will not.

What actually moves the needle

Hook strength. The first line or first two seconds decides whether anyone keeps going. This matters more than any posting slot.

Format fit. Matching the content to what the platform's algorithm currently favors (short video, carousels, native text) outweighs timing by a wide margin.

Consistency of cadence. Showing up on a predictable schedule builds audience habit — people start checking for you, which matters more than which hour you hit publish.

So when should you post?

Whenever you can maintain a sustainable rhythm. Pick a time that fits your workflow and stick with it long enough to gather your own data, rather than copying someone else's chart.
